name: Timaeus
overview: Timaeus is a male figure identified in the New Testament as the father of Bartimaeus. Beyond this familial connection, Scripture provides no additional details about his tribe or other personal attributes. His mention is brief but serves to establish the identity of his son within the Gospel narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Timaeus appears only once in the New Testament, specifically in Mark 10:46. No special meaning or divine origin is attributed to this proper name within the biblical text, and it is presented plainly without additional titles or significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records that Timaeus is the father of Bartimaeus, a relationship inferred from the naming convention found in Mark 10:46. No other familial relationships are documented for him in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: Timaeus is significant primarily as the father of Bartimaeus, the blind beggar who calls out to Jesus for mercy. His mention in the Gospel of Mark helps to authenticate and personalize the account of Bartimaeus's encounter with Christ, underscoring the real-life context of those who sought Jesus's healing power. Though Timaeus himself does not appear directly in the narrative, his identification contributes to the historical grounding of the Gospel account.
